arxiv-2106-10709.title: Spatial Covariance Matrix Reconstruction for DOA Estimation in Hybrid Massive MIMO Systems with Multiple Radio Frequency Chains
arxiv-2106-10709.creator: Yinsheng Liu, Yiwei Yan, Li You, Wenji Wang, Hongtao Duan
arxiv-2106-10709.description: Abstract Multiple signal classification (MUSIC) has been widely applied in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) receivers for direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation. To reduce the cost of radio frequency (RF) chains operating at millimeter-wave bands, hybrid analog-digital structure has been adopted in massive MIMO transceivers.

arxiv-2208-07582.title: Deletion Robust Non-Monotone Submodular Maximization over Matroids
arxiv-2208-07582.creator: Paul DüttingFederico Fusco, Silvio Lattanzi, Ashkan Norouzi-Fard, Morteza Zadimoghaddam
arxiv-2208-07582.description: Abstract Maximizing a submodular function is a fundamental task in machine learning and in this paper we study the deletion robust version of the problem under the classic matroids constraint. Here the goal is to extract a small size summary of the dataset that contains a high value independent set even after an adversary deleted some elements.

arxiv-2209-00696.title: Towards Gravity From a Color Symmetry
arxiv-2209-00696.creator: Alfredo Guevara
arxiv-2209-00696.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Alfredo Guevara. Using tools from color-kinematics duality we propose a holographic construction of gravitational amplitudes, based on a 2d Kac-Moody theory on the celestial sphere. In the N → ∞ N\to\infty limit the gauge group corresponds to w 1 + ∞ w_{1+\infty} , due to the U ⁡ ( N ) U(N) generators enjoying a simple quantum group structure, which is in turn inherited from a twistor fiber over the celestial sphere.

arxiv-2312-01180.title: A Comparative Analysis of Text-to-Image Generative AI Models in Scientific Contexts: A Case Study on Nuclear Power Journal: a Journal (Under Review)
arxiv-2312-01180.creator: Veda Joynt a,★ , Jacob Cooper a,★ , Naman Bhargava b,★ , Katie Vu c,★ , O Hwang Kwon a,★ , Todd R. Allen a , Aditi Verma a , Majdi I. Radaideh a,∗, ★ Authors who have contributed equally to this manuscript
arxiv-2312-01180.description: Abstract In this work, we propose and assess the potential of generative artificial intelligence (AI) to generate public engagement around potential clean energy sources. Such an application could increase energy literacy – an awareness of low-carbon energy sources among the public therefore leading to increased participation in decision-making about the future of energy systems.

arxiv-2406-00514.title: Evolution of the rotating Rayleigh-Taylor instability under the influence of magnetic fields.
arxiv-2406-00514.creator: Narinder Singh 1 and Anikesh Pal 1
arxiv-2406-00514.description: Abstract The combined effects of the imposed vertical mean magnetic field ( B 0 B_{0} , scaled as the Alfvèn velocity) and rotation on the heat transfer phenomenon driven by the Rayleigh-Taylor (RT) instability are investigated using direct numerical simulations.

arxiv-2410-14204.title: MediTOD: An English Dialogue Dataset for Medical History Taking with Comprehensive Annotations
arxiv-2410-14204.creator: Vishal Vivek Saley, Goonjan Saha, Rocktim Jyoti Das, Dinesh Raghu, Mausam
arxiv-2410-14204.description: Abstract Medical task-oriented dialogue systems can assist doctors by collecting patient medical history, aiding in diagnosis, or guiding treatment selection, thereby reducing doctor burnout and expanding access to medical services. However, doctor-patient dialogue datasets are not readily available, primarily due to privacy regulations.

arxiv-2502-03253.title: How do Humans and Language Models Reason About Creativity? A Comparative Analysis
arxiv-2502-03253.creator: Antonio Laverghetta Jr. Tuhin Chakrabarty Tom Hope Jimmy Pronchick Krupa Bhawsar Roger E. Beaty
arxiv-2502-03253.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Antonio Laverghetta Jr. Tuhin Chakrabarty Tom Hope Jimmy Pronchick Krupa Bhawsar Roger E. Beaty. Creativity assessment in science and engineering is increasingly based on both human and AI judgment, but the cognitive processes and biases behind these evaluations remain poorly understood.

arxiv-2512-05379.title: Mitigating Self-Preference by Authorship Obfuscation
arxiv-2512-05379.creator: Taslim Mahbub, Shi Feng
arxiv-2512-05379.description: Abstract Language models (LMs) judges are widely used to evaluate the quality of LM outputs. Despite many advantages, LM judges display concerning biases that can impair their integrity in evaluations. One such bias is self-preference: LM judges preferring their own answers over those produced by other LMs or humans.

pmc-11359576.creator: Griffin C Sipes, Matthew Lee, Kellie M Halloran, Ian Rice, Mariana E Kersh, Shyqyri Haxha
pmc-11359576.description: The increased risk of cardiovascular disease in people with spinal cord injuries motivates work to identify exercise options that improve health outcomes without causing risk of musculoskeletal injury. Handcycling is an exercise mode that may be beneficial for wheelchair users, but further work is needed to establish appropriate guidelines and requires assessment of the external loads.

pmc-11634440.title: Regular whole blood donation and gastrointestinal, breast, colorectal and haematological cancer risk among blood donors in Australia
pmc-11634440.creator: Md Morshadur Rahman, Andrew Hayen, John K. Olynyk, Anne E. Cust, David O. Irving, Surendra Karki
pmc-11634440.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background and ObjectivesSeveral studies have suggested that blood donors have lower risk of gastrointestinal and breast cancers, whereas some have indicated an increased risk of haematological cancers. We examined these associations by appropriately adjusting the ‘healthy donor effect’ (HDE).Materials and MethodsWe examined the risk of gastrointestinal/colorectal, breast and haematological cancers in regular high‐frequency whole blood (WB) donors using the Sax Institute's 45 and Up Study data linked with blood donation and other health‐related data.

pmc-12382067.title: Integration of genome and transcriptome reveals core genes and allele-specific expression genetic variants associated with immune differentiation of taurine ancestry dairy cattle from indicine ancestry cattle
pmc-12382067.creator: Quanzhen Chen, Siqian Chen, Yongjie Tang, Qingyao Zhao, Xilai Zhu, Li Zhi, Xiao Feng, Huaming Mao, Kaixing Qu, Ying Yu
pmc-12382067.description: BackgroundDisease is a key factor to shorten productive lifespan of dairy cattle. Shifting from classical ‘treating existing diseases’ to ‘preventing diseases before they occur’ is a challenge in high-producing dairy cattle. Immunity plays a crucial role in defending against disease. Substantial evidence indicates that the immune function of taurine ancestry cattle and indicine ancestry cattle are distinct.

pmc-13258530.title: The expression and clinical significance of miR-635 and miR-519d in gastric cancer patients
pmc-13258530.creator: Jinjin Liu, Qiuping Gu, Cixiang Chen, Xiaohui Liu
pmc-13258530.description: ObjectiveTo investigate the expression and clinical significance of miR-635 and miR-519d in patients with gastric cancer.MethodsA total of 116 patients with gastric cancer admitted between July 2018 and July 2020 were enrolled. Gastric cancer tissues and matched adjacent tissues obtained during surgery were collected. The expression levels of miR-635 and miR-519d were detected by quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR).

pmc-13380734.creator: Felix Ampadu, Nikhil Patil, Venkateswararao Eeda, Iulia Rus, Woncheol Jung, Hassan M Abu shukair, Anza Ali, Yuriana Aguilar-Sanchez, Tae Gyu Oh, Vibhudutta Awasthi, Aditya D Joshi

pmc-13527537.title: Artificial Intelligence Integration With Nanotechnology for Cancer Therapy
pmc-13527537.creator: Shengbin Liu, Zhi Liu, Haixing Shi, Chengyi Wei, Ruijie Zhang, Xiangrong Song
pmc-13527537.description: Cancer nanomedicine offers a versatile platform for improving therapeutic index, but its clinical translation remains limited by unpredictable in vivo behavior, heterogeneous biological contexts, and inefficient design paradigms.
